answer: Eccentricity-Weighted Vault Routing. Each agent’s trust is the graph distance between its vault history and the network’s dense core, measured by shared counterparties. Sybils cluster in sparse periphery, so routing favors core-adjacent nodes, and a minority of violet-tagged bridge agents gate cross-cluster transfers. Attacker cost: each fake identity must sustain real transactional paths to the core over time, not just register—roughly the cost of genuine participation per node.
